summary: AUDIT-2-2 (webhook secret encryption + return-once) grilled against the confirmed audit finding and the existing external-ingress encryption pattern it must reuse. No new architecture: the runtime keyring already encrypts ingress secrets; this applies the same to webhook secrets.
gaps: Encryption must not change the delivered HMAC signature (downstream consumers depend on byte-compatibility).
Ciphertext must be bound to appId+webhookId so a swapped row can't decrypt.
Existing plaintext rows must migrate or force rotation.
The generated secret must be returned once at create without leaking on later reads.
resolutions: Decrypt only at the delivery/signing boundary; the HMAC key is the same bytes, so signatures stay identical - pinned by a byte-compatibility test.
Ciphertext binds appId+webhookId as authenticated metadata; wrong-identity decryption fails (test).
Migrate rows via the same path external-ingress used; fail on unencrypted legacy values.
Create returns the generated secret once; list/get/update projections keep omitting it (test).
